title: AW27 Kids' Trim Market Strategy
summary: Durable, safe trims for AW27 kidswear in a cautious market.
research_period: Pitti Filati, June 2026; Première Vision, Lineapelle and Milano Unica, September 2026; forecaster reports to November 2026

sections.heading: How this forecast was built
sections.body: Pre-fair forecast. The AW27 kidswear fairs (Pitti Bimbo and Playtime Paris) take place in January 2027. This report applies the 2026 adult yarn, fabric and leather fair evidence and the AW26 kidswear fair record to kidswear, and will be updated after the fairs.

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
- Fashion is expected to remain in low single-digit growth in 2027, with markdown risk from excess stock<sup>[1]</sup>
- EU Directive 2024/825 bans greenwashing and misleading environmental claims; Italy's transposing decree entered into force on 27 September 2026<sup>[2]</sup>
- At Playtime Paris in January 2026 (AW26 collections), CSR was "no longer a peripheral narrative": Minimalisma uses silk, merino, organic cotton and linen; MarMar Copenhagen uses Tencel modal and organic cotton for clothes that "last"; Gray Label sells a permanent unisex range and runs a pre-loved take-back<sup>[3]</sup>

sections.heading: Build, test, sell through
sections.body:
| Action | Trims |
|---|---|
| Build | Embroidered badges, piping, snaps |
| Test | Character appliqué, fur-effect collars |
| Avoid | Glued decoration, small parts |

design_implications:
- Wash-test all trims.
- Safety: no drawstrings or long cords at the hood, neck or waist, in line with EN 14682; test the attachment strength of buttons, snaps and decorations, and keep small detachable parts off baby and toddler pieces.
commercial_implications: - Do not use unproven eco claims on trims.
